newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-TENDULAR, AZHARUDDIN HIT CENTURIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULAR, AZHARUDDIN HIT CENTURIES.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin completed centuries to put India in a commanding position at tea on the second day of the first test against Sri Lanka on Sunday.
They were 479 for five at the interval with Azharuddin unbeaten on 126. Tendulkar made 143.
The overnight pair put on 221 for the fourth wicket, a record for India in tests against Sri Lanka. It beat the previous highest of 163 by Sunil Gavaskar and Azharuddin at Kanpur in 1986-87.
Their stand was finally ended when Tendulkar lofted off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan to long-on where test debutant Mahela Jayawardena took a fine, running catch.
The Indian captain faced 247 balls and hit 20 fours in his third century against Sri Lanka.
Sri Lanka, who had laboured on a lifeless pitch for almost five hours for a wicket, captured another almost immediately when Saurav Ganguly was dismissed without scoring.
The left-hander attempted to cut left-arm spinner Sanath Jayasuriya and was caught at slip by Roshan Mahanama.
Azharuddin completed his 18th test century, his fourth against Sri Lanka, in 223 minutes off 162 balls with eight fours.
